subject: Territory pay supplement review — offer indexing & COLA bands
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Territory pay supplement review — offer indexing & COLA bands

Hi all,

Quick note to kick off a short review: recruiting is seeing increasing variance in acceptance rates for remote offers across regions. To keep offer economics predictable while being competitive, I drafted a territory-based supplement proposal (attached) that would sit on top of our base bands for remote hires. Key points: 

- Goal: narrow the gap between US nominal bands and local purchasing parity in EU/APAC while keeping overall comp spend within current forecast.
- Proposal: three supplement tiers by territory (Tier A: +0% nominal, Tier B: +6-10%, Tier C: +12-18%) driven by a blended COLA index and market salary comps.
- Example: L4 SWE base remains unchanged in USD banding; for candidates hired in Manila (Tier C) we’d add a +14% supplement at offer time (reflected as a one-line "Territory Supplement" until converted to localized salary in payroll).
- Governance: hiring PM signs off + People Ops finalizes localized payroll mechanics. No retroactive changes for existing offers.

I attached the workbook (intl_col_adjustments_v1.xlsx) and a short APAC market slice. Please review and reply with: accept / request adjustment / need more data by EOD Wednesday (Nov 24).

Open items I flagged in sheet: Singapore cap, and whether we should treat EU remote in EUR or continue paying USD with an FX overlay.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Recruiter, People Operations
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

On Fri, 20 Nov 2026 at 09:12, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick note to kick off a short review: recruiting is seeing increasing variance in acceptance rates for remote offers across regions. 

Thanks Neha — good start. A few quick thoughts inline and below: 

- Singapore: market comps show base salary inflation for SWE L4 is roughly +8-12% vs our USD-converted bands; I think Singapore should be Tier B by default, not Tier C, unless the role is senior-heavy.
- India (Bengaluru): total comp expectations are more nuanced — for a strictly remote hire on local payroll we should use a locally competitive base rather than a pure supplement. For hires on EoR/EOR payroll, the supplement approach is ok but cap at +10%.
- EUR handling: prefer to localize to EUR for hires who will be paid locally (compliance and payroll clarity), but allow USD billing for contractors/short-term engagements.

I edited the spreadsheet with suggested territory assignments and added an "EOR vs Local Payroll" column. Also added suggested cap logic for equity adjustments when supplement exceeds 12%.

LMK if you want me to run the payout modeling against the Q4 headcount plan.

—Karthik

Attachments referenced:
- intl_col_adjustments_v1.xlsx (edited)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Territory pay supplement review — offer indexing & COLA bands

Folks — added some market context from recent offers (SF, Dublin, Singapore, Manila):

- Dublin: candidates are more responsive to guaranteed base than supplements; if cost allows, localizing to EUR + small supplement (4-6%) gets better accept.
- Manila / Philippines: acceptance improved when we show localized total target comp (converted to PHP) rather than a line-item supplement. That said, for speed-to-offer I like a supplement approach with a path to localization at onboarding.
- Singapore cap suggestion: use a soft cap at +15% — above that we should explore leveling to a higher band or offering more equity.

I attached a short APAC market slice (market_slice_apac.pdf) and a draft candidate offer paragraph for territory supplement wording (offer_language_territory_v2.docx).

Proposed next steps:
1) Accept the draft territory tiers with Singapore -> Tier B, Philippines -> Tier C, India split by payroll type.
2) People Ops to draft final payroll/benefits flow for localized hires.
3) Recruiting to pilot on three open reqs this week (SWE L4, PM L3, CS Mgr) and track delta in acceptance.

-Marissa

Attachments:
- market_slice_apac.pdf (pdf)
- offer_language_territory_v2.docx (docx)

Thanks team — appreciate the fast turn. I approve moving forward with the pilot, subject to two caveats:

1) Any supplement >12% requires sign-off from me and People Ops (Priyom) before the offer is extended.
2) We do not change job leveling to force supplements — if market demands higher base, consider repricing to the next band instead of inflating supplements long-term.

Please proceed with the three-pilot hires and include a short one-slide LOE for executive review once we have two outcomes (accept/decline).

Laura
VP, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — looping you in on our internal approach so you have context for the offer coming from Redwood. Below is the short version for Greenwood Health:

- We will present total target comp in local currency where we hire locally. For remote hires in your geography we will apply a "Territory Supplement" line when appropriate (example: Philippines +14%).
- The supplement is visible on the offer as a separate line item and converted to local payroll at onboarding. It is not a bonus and will be included in taxable pay per local rules.
- For Greenwood's candidate (SWE L4) we propose: base band = USD 150k (banded), Territory Supplement = +12% -> total target = USD 168k equivalent (to be converted to PHP for payroll).

Could you confirm Greenwood's preference for payroll (Greenwood local payroll vs Redwood-contracted EOR) so we can finalize the mechanics and send the formal offer? If you prefer our EOR, we will bill in USD and keep the supplement at the percentage level; if you prefer local payroll, we will present localized currency and finalize gross pay with your payroll team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
Neha
